english: “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with dressed stones; the sycamores have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place” (Isaiah 9:10)

twi: COVID-19 yadeɛ kontonkurowi ho nsunsuansoɔ bɔne no aka ewiase ɔman biara sikasɛm a Ghanaman ka ho bi.
english: The devastating impact of the COVID-19 pandemic has been felt by all economies, including Ghana.

twi: Ahohiahia a ɛkɔwiee owuo, asetenam ahokyere ne adwumasɛeɛ a Ghanafoɔ hunuiɛ no nyɛ adeɛ a Aban werɛ afiri koraa.
english: The hardship experienced by Ghanaians through the loss of lives, livelihoods and businesses is not lost on the Government.

twi: Mede ahohoahoa ka sɛ anammɔn a ɔman yi tuu wɔ yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi ho no yɛ akokoɔduru anammɔn na ɛyɛ gyinaeɛsie a ɛdi mu pa ara a ewiase aman nyinaa agye atom sɛ yɛayɛ adeɛ.
english: I am proud to say that our response to address the impact of the pandemic was bold and decisive and has been admired all over the world.

twi: Aban sane yɛɛ nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ nam so boaa ankorankorɛ nnwuma sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a ɔmanfoɔ bɛsane asi wɔn dada mu.
english: Government also initiated policies to help revive businesses and bring our lives back to normalcy.

twi: Deɛ ɛdi hɔ bio nso ne sɛ, sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛtumi agyina ɔhaw ne akwannya ahodoɔ a yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi de aba no ano enti, Aban nam Ɔmanpanin Nana Addo Ghana Dankwa Akufo-Addo mpaninnie a ɛdi mu no so de ahoɔherɛ hyehyɛɛ Covid- (GhanaCARES) 19 Asetɔre Ne Ankorankorɛ Nnwuma Mu Nkanyan Ho Mmoa "Obaatan Pa- Dwumadie (Ghana COVID-19 Alleviation and Revitalisation of Enterprises programme, (the GhanaCARES “Obaatan Pa” programme) a emu (GH¢100 billion) sikabotene yɛ sidi ɔpepepem ɔha baako .
english: Further, in response to the threats and opportunities arising out of the pandemic, Government, under the able leadership of H.E. President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo- Addo, quickly developed a GH¢100 billion COVID-19 Alleviation and Revitalisation of Enterprises programme, (the GhanaCARES “Obaatan Pa” programme). This has brought instant and significant relief to our people and is revitalising our nation.

twi: Yei de ahomegyeɛ mapa mu. abrɛ yɛn nkurɔfoɔ na ɛgu so de nkanyan reba ɔman no ɔyɛ yɛn ahomeka sɛ mogu so wɔ gyidie wɔ Aban mu wɔ ɛberɛ a yɛgu so reyɛ biribiara a ɛhia de ama yɛade yɛ ho afiri yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi ho. ɔnam deɛ ɛtoo yɛn wɔ saa ɛberɛ no mu no so ama yɛahunu sɛdeɛ yɛn nsiyɛ sɛ ɔman a yɛtumi gyina atoyerɛnkyɛm ano no teɛ.
english: We appreciate your keeping faith with Government even as we work to ensure a strong recovery from the pandemic. Through this period, our resilience to survive as a nation has been tested.

twi: Twerɛ Kronkron no ma yɛn akwankyerɛ ɛberɛ biara a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛfa so wɔ mmerɛ a ɛte sei mu wɔ Yesaia nwoma, etire 9, nkyekyɛmu 10 hɔ a wɔatwerɛ sɛ, “Berekese no adwiri agu fam, nanso yɛde aboɔ a wɔatwa bɛto bio; wɔatwitwa borɔdɔma nnua no Saa ara na Aban asi nkete sɛ ɔbɛdi ne agu nanso yɛde ntweneduro bɛhyɛ anan mu.” bɔhyɛ nyinaa so na ne saa enti, ɔbɛkɔ so ayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ na wadi dwuma ahodoɔ a ɛbɛma yɛn nsa aka deɛ yɛahwere nyinaa na ɛnam so ama ɔmanfoɔ asetenam atu mpɔn.
english: In particular, as stated in Isaiah 9.10, “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with dressed stones; the sycamores have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place”. In the same vein, Government is equally determined to deliver on its promises.

twi: Botaeɛ ahodoɔ no mu baako a ɛdi akotene wɔ 2022 Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi mu ɛnna afei wɔ mfeɛ mmiɛnsa a ɛdi yɛn anim yi mu ne sɛ, yɛbɛkyekyere Ɔman a Ankorankorɛ Nnwumabue ase bɛtim wɔ mu na ɛbɛma yɛn sikasɛm kankorɔ adi mu, na obiara bɛdi ne dwuma sɛdeɛ ɛfata na ɛnam so ama nnwuma abu so na ne titire, mmabunu anya bi ayɛ.
english: One of the key objectives of the 2022 Budget, and indeed for the next three (3) years, is to build a sustainable Entrepreneurial State capable of delivering economic growth that is robust, sustainable, and inclusive to generate decent work for all, particularly the Youth.

twi: Yei enti, Aban nhyehyɛeɛ a ɔbɛtu ho anammɔn no bɛyɛ deɛ ɛbɛboa mmabunu, nam so ahunu adom akyɛdeɛ a wɔwɔ na yɛaboa ama obiara anya akwannya de adi dwuma sɛdeɛ ɛbɛboa ama ahonya aba ama obiara.
english: Government policies will, therefore, be geared towards supporting the youth to exploit their talents and unleash their potential to ensure prosperity through equal opportunity for all.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛma mmabunu anya nkuranhyɛ na wɔanya nnnwumabue sunsum de abuebue wɔn ankasa nnwuma enti, afe 2022 mu no, Aban bɛhyɛ dwumadie bi a YouStart yɛato edin Nhyehyɛeɛ ase a ɛnam so bɛma mmabunu anya bosea de ahyɛ aseɛ abuebue wɔn nnwuma na atumi agyina anaa wɔde atrɛ wɔn nnwuma mu.
english: To boost the confidence of the youth and build their entrepreneurial spirit, Government will activate the YouStart programme in 2022 to provide access to credit for young businesses persons to either establish or expand their business.

twi: Afe 2022 Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi mu no, yɛayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ a yɛde bɛtoa so atu anammɔn wɔ ɔman yi mu ɔhaw ahodoɔ a yɛwɔ mu seesei no ho nam so ama yɛatumi agyina yɛn nan so bio wɔ yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi akyi.
english: In the 2022 Budget, we have outlined plans to continue to tackle the immediate challenges of the economy and to emerge stronger in the post-pandemic era.

twi: Aban de asi n’ani so sɛ ɔbɛyɛ ntotoeɛ a ɛdi mu na ɔne akuhodoɔ adi nsawɔsoɔ de atu anammɔn a ɛbɛma mmabunu anya nsaanonnwuma ho nteteeɛ na yɛahwɛ ama ankorankorɛ nnwumabue atu mpɔn wɔ mmabunu mu. ɔberɛ a yɛgu so redi dwuma wɔ Ɔmanpanin anisoadehunu a ɔpɛ sɛ Ghana duru mpɛmpɛnsoɔ a yɛrenhia mmoa (Ghana Beyond Aid) ho no, mɛsrɛ Ghanafoɔ nyinaa, titire mmabubu no sɛ wɔnhunu sɛ wɔwɔ kyɛfa wɔ ɔman yi mu, wɔnsusu biribi pa na wɔmfa wɔn ho nhyɛ ankorankorɛ nnwumabue ɔman a yɛrekyekyere ama aseɛ atim no mu na ɛnwie pɛyɛ.
english: Government is dedicated to comprehensive and coordinated initiatives to provide skills and promote entrepreneurship amongst the youth. As we pursue the President's ” vision of moving Ghana Beyond Aid, I wish to appeal to all Ghanaians, particularly the Youth to assume this shared ownership, be innovative, and be actively involved in building a sustainable Entrepreneurial State.

twi: Mehyɛ yɛn nyinaa nkuran sɛ yɛmmoa na yɛnkyekyere Ghanaman a yɛn nyinaa hwehwɛ no.
english: I charge us all to help build the Ghana we desire.

twi: Onyankopɔn nhyira yɛnƆƆƆƆ Ken Ofori-Atta Ɔsoafoɔ a ɔhwɛ Sikasɛm so
english: Minister for Finance ”

twi: Afe 2022 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi yɛ dwuma a Aban dii wɔ 2021 mu no ho tɔfabɔ ne sika dodoɔ a Aban hwɛ anim sɛ ɔbɛnya de atu ne nhyehyɛeɛ ne ne dwumadie ahodoɔ ho anammɔn wɔ afe 2022 mu ne mmerɛ kakra a ɛdi yɛn anim yi mu.
english: The 2022 Citizen's Budget is a summary of what Government achieved in 2021 and how much the Government intends to collect in revenues to implement its policies and programmes in 2022 and the medium-term.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na anammɔn a yɛretu ama asetenam ne sikasɛm mpontuo asane apagya na ɔman mpontuo botaeɛ ahodoɔ abam no enti, afe 2022 Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi botaeɛ ne sɛ yɛbɛfa Sikasɛm Ntotoeɛ pa so bɛkyekyere Ɔman a Ankorankorɛ Nnwumabue ase bɛtim wɔ mu na Nnwuma abu so ama ɔman mma anya bi ayɛ.
english: To support socio-economic recovery efforts and national development goals, the 2022 Budget focuses on Building a Sustainable Entrepreneurial Nation through Fiscal Consolidation and Job Creation.

twi: Sɛdeɛ na Ɔman sikasɛm mu mpontuo nnyinasoɔ no teɛ 3. Deɛ ɛdidi soɔ yi yɛ nkontabuo ho amaneɛbɔ a yɛn nsa aka a ɛkyerɛ sɛdeɛ na ɔman sikasɛm teɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu:
english: Provisional data on the performance of the economy in 2021 is as follows.

twi: Abosome nsia a na ɛdi kan wɔ afe 2021 mu no, ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ nyinaa mu mpontuo duruu ɔha mu nkyɛmu mmiɛnsa ne akyire pɔ mmiɛnsa (Overall real GDP averaged 3.5 %) wɔ ɛberɛ a na saa ɛberɛ korɔ no ara mu wɔ afe 2020 mu no, adwadeɛ mu mpontuo duruu ɔha mu nkyɛmu hwee ne akyire pɔ nson (0.7 % growth), Non-Oil real GDP) kɔɔ Adwadeɛ a ɛma yɛnya sika a Fango nka ho ( anim ɔha mu nkyɛmu ɛnan ne akyire pɔ nwɔtwe (4.8 %) wɔ abosome nsia a ɛdi kan wɔ afe 2021 mu, na saa ɛberɛ korɔ no ara mu wɔ afe 2020 mu no, saa sika yi kɔɔ anim ɔha mu nkyɛmu baako ne akyre pɔ baako pɛ (1.1 %), Na nneɛma boɔ-sorokɔ wɔ ɔbɔ bosome awieeɛ yɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu (10.6 %), na saa ɛberɛ korɔ no ara wɔ afe 2020 edu ne akyire pɔ nsia mu no, na nneɛma boɔ-sorokɔ yɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu edu ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (10.4 %), Sika dodoɔ a na aka mu a yɛhia de asɔ yɛn sikasɛm nhyehyɛeɛ mu Overall budget deficit -cash) wɔ abosome nsia a ɛdi sika nyinaa so ( kan wɔ afe 2021 mu no yɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu nson ne akyire pɔ nson 7.7 % of GDP), na saa ɛberɛ korɔ no ara mu wɔ afe 2020 mu no, na deɛ ɛsi yɛn ani so yɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu nson ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (7.4 % of GDP), Primary balance) Sika dodoɔ a yɛbɛhia de atua dwumadie ho ɛka ( no 2.0 % of GDP), na yɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu mmienu ne akyire pɔ hwee ( saa ɛberɛ korɔ no ara wɔ afe 2020 mu no, na ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu baako ne akyire pɔ nson (1.7. %), Ɛka a na ɔman no de a wode ba ɔman adwadeɛ nyinaa mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu (%age of GDP) a, ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduoson nson ne akyire pɔ nson (77.7 %) wɔ Ɛbɔ bosome awieeɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu, wɔ ɛberɛ a Ɔpɛnimma bosome baa awieeɛ wɔ afe 2020 mu no, na ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduoson nsia ne akyire pɔ baako (76.1 %), (Gross International Reserves) Amannɔne Sika Dodoɔ a Ɔman no wɔ nso kɔduruu Amɛrika sika ɔpepepem dubaako ne ɔpepem aduanan US$11.44 billion) wɔ Ɔsanaa bosome awieeɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu, ɛnan ( a ɛbɛtumi akra nneɛma abosome enum ne nnanu na wode toto Ɔpɛnimma bosome awieeɛ wɔ afe 2020 mu ho a, na ɛyɛ Amɛrika sika ɔpepepem nwɔtwe ne ɔpepem aduosia mmienu (US$8.62 billion) a na ɛbɛtumi akra nneɛma abosome ɛnan ne da koro pɛ, ɛnna afei Ɔman no sika ahoɔden wɔ amannɔne sika atitire mu no gyinaa faako kama wɔ afe 2021 mu. Ɛduruu Ɛbɔ bosome awieeɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu no, na Ghana sika no ahoɔden wɔ Amɛrika sika mu apagya bɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu baako ne akyire pɔ nson (1.7% against the US Dollar) na wode toto saa ɛberɛ korɔ no ara ho wɔ afe 2020 mu a, ɔman no sika ahoɔden wɔ Amɛrika sika mu no so tee ɔha mu nkyɛmu mmienu ne akyire pɔ nkron (2.9 % depreciation).
english: Overall real GDP averaged 3.5 percent in the first half of 2021 against the 0.7 percent growth in same period 2020; Non-Oil real GDP grew at an average of 4.8 percent in the first half year of 2021 compared to 1.1 percent in the same period 2020; Inflation as at end-September was 10.6 percent, compared to the 10.4 percent same period in 2020; Overall budget deficit (cash) of 7.7 percent of GDP against the target of 7.4 percent of GDP; Primary balance recorded a deficit of 2.0 percent of GDP, compared to the target deficit of 1.7. percent; The Public debt (as percentage of GDP) stood at 77.7 percent at the end of September 2021, up from 76.1 percent at the end of December Gross International Reserves at end-August 2021 was US$11.44 billion, enough to cover 5.2 months of imports, compared to US$8.62 billion equivalent to 4.1 months of imports recorded at end-December 2020; and Exchange rates remained stable across the major international currencies for the three quarters of 2021. Specifically, the Ghana cedi depreciated cumulatively by 1.7 percent against the US Dollar by the end of September 2021, compared to a 2.9 percent depreciation in the same period in 2020.

twi: Sika A Ɛbaa Ɔman Fotoɔ Mu 4. Sika a Aban gyegyee ne deɛ wɔde kyɛɛ ɔman no firi Ɔpɛpɔn kɔsi Ɛbɔ bosome mu wɔ afe 2021 mu no nyinaa kɔsii ɔpepepem aduanan nsia ne ɔpepem aduɔwɔtwe enum (GH¢46.85 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman mu adwadeɛ nyinaa mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu edu ne akyire pɔ nson (10.7% of GDP), na yɛyɛɛ dwumadie mu nsakraeɛ no, na sika dodoɔ a yɛde yɛn ani asi so sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ yɛnya no yɛ ɔpepepem aduonum baako ne ɔpepem aduasa baako (GH¢51.31 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman mu adwadeɛ nyinaa mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu dubaako ne akyire pɔ nson (11.7% of GDP).
english: Total Revenue and Grants for the period January to September 2021 amounted to GH¢46.85 billion (10.70 of GDP), against the revised programme target of GH¢51.31 billion (11.70 of GDP).

twi: Sika dodoɔ a ɛbaa ɔman fotoɔ mu no na ɛdidi soɔ yi: Ɛtoɔ a ɛmfiri fango dwumadie ho sika mu (Non-oil Tax Revenue) a ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduoson ɛnan (74%), sika a ɛmfiri fango mu na ɛnyɛ ɛtoɔ sika (Nonoil-non-Tax Revenue) a ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu nkron (9%), sika a ɛfiri Fango ne Ogyaframa mu (Oil and Gas Receipts) a ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu nkron (9%), sika afoforɔ (other Revenue) a ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu nsia (6%) ɛnna sika a wɔde kyɛɛ ɔman no (Grants) a ɛyɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu mmienu (2%) sɛdeɛ yɛada no adi wɔ Hyehyɛpono 1 mu no.
english: The total revenues received is made up of Non-oil Tax Revenue (740), Non-Oil Non-Tax Revenue (90), Oil and Gas Receipts (90), other Revenue (60) and Grants (20) as seen in Figure 1.

twi: Afe 2021 Sika dodoɔ a Aban gyegyee no annuru deɛ yɛde sii yɛn ani so sɛ yɛn nsa bɛka no ɛsiane sɛ Nnwumakuo Mfasoɔ ho Ɛtoɔ (Corporate Income Tax), Ankorankorɛ Sika ho Ɛtoɔ (Personal Income Tax), Fagudeɛ ho Ɛtoɔ, Ɔman yi mu Adwadeɛ ho Ɛtoɔ (Domestic Excise Duty) ne Nkratoɔ Dwumadie ho Ɛtoɔ (Communications Service Tax) nyinaa so teeɛ.
english: The reduction in total revenue and grants in 2021 compared to the targets was due to lower-than-expected performance in Corporate Income Tax, Personal Income Tax, Mineral Royalties, Domestic Excise Duty, and Communications Service Tax.

twi: Dwuma A Yɛde Sika Diiɛ 6. Ɛbɔ bosome kɔɔ awieeɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu no, na Sika dodoɔ a Aban de adi dwuma (a ɛka a yɛatua ka ho bi) no aduru Ghana sika sidi ɔpepepem aduɔwɔtwe ne ɔpepem aduoson baako (GH¢80.71 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu dunwɔtwe ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (18.4% of GDP) a wode toto dwumadie mu nsakraeɛ a yɛyɛɛ no ho a, na ɛsɛ sɛ anka yɛde Ghana sika sidi ɔpepepem aduɔwɔtwe mmiɛnsa ne ɔpepem aduɔwɔtwe nkron (GH¢83.89 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu dunkron ne akyire pɔ baako (19.1% of GDP) na ɛdi dwuma.
english: Total Government Expenditures (including arrears clearance) as at end September 2021 amounted to GH¢80.71 billion (18.40 of GDP) against the revised target of GH¢83.89 billion (19.10 of GDP).

twi: Adwumayɛfoɔ akatua ne Nsiho-tua na na ɛyɛ nneɛma mmienu a Aban bɔɔ ho ɛka pa ara.
english: Compensation of Employees and Interest Payments were the two biggest expenditure items.

twi: Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ ho Anammɔntuo ne Dwumadie ho Sikapɛ 7. Sika dodoɔ a Aban de dii dwuma boroo so ma ɛka a ɛbaa so yɛ ɔpepepem aduasa mmiɛnsa ne ɔpepem aduɔwɔtwe nsia (GH¢33.86 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu nson ne akyire pɔ nson (7.7% of GDP) a na anka ɛsɛ sɛ ɛyɛ ɔpepepem aduasa mmienu ne ɔpepem aduonum nwɔtwe (GH¢32.58 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu nson ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (7.4% of GDP).
english: Government's fiscal operations resulted in a cash deficit of GH¢33.86 billion (7.70 of GDP), compared to the revised target of GH¢32.58 billion (7.40 of GDP).

twi: Aban pɛɛ ɛka a ɛboroo so yi ho sika firii ɔman yi mu ne amannɔne.
english: The deficit was financed from both domestic and external sources.

twi: Sika dodoɔ a Aban nyaa no wɔ ɔman yi mu no kɔduruu ɔpepepem aduonu ne ɔpepem aduasa nkron (GH¢20.39 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduosia ne akyire pɔ mmienu (60.2% of GDP) na sika a Aban nya firii amannɔne nso kɔduruu ɔpepepem dumiɛnsa ne ɔpepem aduanan nson (GH¢13.47 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ ɔha mu

twi: Ɛka A Ɔman Bɔɔ Wɔ afe 2021 Mu 8. twi: Nneɛma a ɛma Ɔman sikasɛm gyina a yɛde ani abu sɛ yɛbɛnya wɔ 2022 mu 9. Ɔman sikasɛm nnyinasoɔ a ɛddi soɔ yi na yɛde yɛn ani abu sɛ yɛn nsa bɛka wɔ afe 2022 mu: Ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ nyinaa kankorɔ ɔha mu nkyɛmu enum ne akyire pɔ nwɔtwe (Real GDP growth of 5.8 %), Ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ a Fango nka ho bie kankorɔ ɔha mu nkyɛmu enum akyire pɔ nkron (Non-Oil Real GDP growth of 5.9 %), Ɔpɛnimma bosome awieeɛ nneɛma boɔ-sorokɔ ɔha mu nkyɛmu nwɔtwe (End-December inflation of 8 %), Sika a yɛbɛdi aboro deɛ yɛwɔ so- ɔha mu nkyɛmu nson ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (Fiscal deficit of 7.4 % of GDP), Sika dodoɔ a ɛbɛboro deɛ yɛbɛgyegyeɛ so- ɔha mu nkyɛmu hwee ne akyire pɔ baako (Primary surplus of 0.1 % of GDP), ɛnna Amannɔne Sika Dodoɔ a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛnya de kra nneɛma bɛyɛ abosome ɛnan.
english: The following macroeconomic targets have been set for 2022. Overall Real GDP growth of 5.8 percent; Non-Oil Real GDP growth of 5.9 percent; End-December inflation of 8 percent; Fiscal deficit of 7.4 percent of GDP; Primary surplus of 0.1 percent of GDP; and Gross International Reserves to cover not less than 4 months of imports.

twi: Ɛkwan a yɛbɛfa so apɛ sika wɔ 10. Aban ani da ɛkwan sɛ sika dodoɔ a ɔbɛtumi agyegye ne deɛ wɔde bɛkyɛ yɛn wɔ afe 2022 mu no nyinaa bɛduru Ghana sika sidi ɔpepepem ɔha ne ɔpepem mmienu (GH¢100.52 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ mu ɔha mu aduonum nkyɛmu aduonu ne akyire pɔ (20.0 % of GDP).

english: Domestic Revenue is estimated at GH¢99.55 billion.

english: Of the total Domestic Revenue amount, Non-oil Tax Revenue constitutes 77.5 percent and amounts to GH¢77.136 million.

english: The resource mobilisation for 2022 is expected to be impacted by improvements in tax compliance, reforms in revenue administration, as well as tax policy measures.

twi: Sɛdeɛ yɛbɛkyekyɛ sika mu wɔ afe 11. Aban ayɛ adwene sɛ sika dodoɔ a ɔde bɛdi dwuma (a ɛka a yɛbɛtua ka ho bi) bɛduru Ghana sika sidi ɔpepepem ɔha aduasa nson ne ɔpepem aduonum mmiɛnsa (GH¢137.53 billion) a ɛyɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduonu nson ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (27.4 % of GDP).
english: Total Expenditure (including clearance of Arrears) is projected at GH¢137.53 billion (27.4 percent of GDP). key drivers of the expenditure growth include Capital Expenditure, funding of Government flagship programmes, wage bill, and interest payments.

twi: Ɔman Sikanya Ho Nhyehyɛeɛ Ahodoɔ 14. Aban de nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ agu akwan mu a ɛnam so bɛkanyan mfidinnwuma na aboa ama wɔayɛ adwadeɛ a ɛdi mu a ɛbɛnya edwa wɔ ɔman yi mu ne amannɔne.
english: Government will introduce measures that will revamp industry and make their products competitive in both the local and international markets.

twi: Ne saa enti, ɛho akɔhia sɛ yɛyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ mu nsakraeɛ ahodoɔ a ɛdidi soɔ yi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛma mfasoɔ a ɛbɛba mfidinnwuma mu no ase atim na wɔatumi atrɛ wɔn dwumadie mu enti, Aban de mfeɛ mmienu bɛka mmerɛ dodoɔ a ɔde maa ntomatam mfidinnwuma sɛ wɔrentua adwadeɛyɔ ho ɛtoɔ (Vat Relief) no a ɔhyɛɛ aseɛ wɔ afe 2019 mu no ho, Mfeɛ mmienu akyi nie a yɛde amannɔne edwadie nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛfa nneɛma a yɛkra firi amannɔne ho dii dwuma a emu no, yɛmaa amannɔne adwadifoɔ kɔn mu dwoo wɔn kakra.
english: In this respect, it has become increasingly necessary to make the following policy changes.

twi: Yɛbɛyɛ nsakraeɛ wɔ saa nhyehyɛeɛ yi mu ama adi mu na aboa amannɔne adwadifoɔ pɔtee a ɛsɛ sɛ saa nhyehyɛeɛ yi boa wɔn no, Yɛbɛte ɛtoɔ a fagudeɛtuo nnwuma nketewa a wɔtɔn sikakɔkɔɔ a yɛmfa mfaa afidie mu tua no so firi ɔha mu nkyɛmu mmiɛnsa de akɔ ɔha mu nkyɛmu baako ne ɛfa (withholding tax rate reduction from 3 % to 1.5 Ɛfiri Ɔpɛpɔn ahyɛaseɛ wɔ afe 2022 mu no, Ghana Ɛtoɔgyeɛ Adwumakuo (Ghana Revenue Authority) bɛboa Nkuropɔn, Nkuro ne Mansini Mmarahyɛbadwa (MMDAs) no ama wɔapɛ akwannya korɔ a ɛbɛboa wɔn ama wɔatu anammɔn wɔ ntokuatoɔ gyegyeɛ ntotoeɛ ho ama wɔatumi agyegye no yie na wɔabu ho nkonta pa nso, Aban bɛyɛ nsakraeɛ wɔ sika ahodoɔ a Aban Nnwuma Ahodoɔ (MDAs) gye wɔ wɔn dwumadie ho no mu na ahyɛ aseɛ ayɛ adwuma firi Ɔpɛpɔn da a ɛdi kan wɔ afe 2022 mu.
english: To consolidate gains and expand production in the industry, Government will extend the Vat Relief introduced on African textile prints for textile manufacturers in 2019 for a further two years; After two and a half years of operation, the temporal benchmark (discount) policy on imports introduced as a stop-gap measure will be reviewed to make it more efficient and targeted; Reduction in withholding tax rate for sale of unprocessed gold by smallscale miners on whom the incidence of tax falls from 3 percent to 1.5 percent; Starting from January 2022, Government, through the Ghana Revenue Authority, will assist MMDAs to implement a common platform for property tax administration to enhance Property tax collections and its accountability; Government will review fees and charges of MDAs for implementation from 1st January, 2022. Fees and charges will be subjected to automatic adjustment consistent with the annual average inflation rate; There will be zero-rate tolls on all public roads and bridges effective immediately the Budget is approved.

twi: Sika ahodoɔ a Aban Nnwuma gyegye mu nsakraeɛ no bɛgyina sɛdeɛ afe biara nneɛma-boɔ sorokɔ no teɛ so, Mmarahyɛbadwafoɔ gye Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi tom ara pɛ, ntɛm pa ara lɔrekwan so ɛtoɔ a yɛtua no bɛba awieeɛ, Yɛde Abɛɛfo Afidie so Sikamaneɛ ho Ɛtoɔ ("Electronic Transaction Levyanaa "E-Levy-) bɛba sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a ɛbɛma ɛtoɔtua mu atrɛ na ama wɔn a wɔn din nni Aban nwoma mu nso abɛka nnipa a wɔtua ɛtoɔ wɔ ɔman yi mu no ho.
english: There will be an introduction of “Electronic Transaction levy” or “Elevy” on all electronic transactions to widen the tax net and rope in the informal sector.

twi: Saa ɛtoɔ yi bɛka “fonq so sikamaneɛ, sikakorabea sikamaneɛ, “fonq so sikamaneɛ ho dwumadie ne sikamaneɛ a ɛfiri amannɔne, na ɛtoɔ a ɛda so yɛ ɔha mu nkyɛmu baako ne akyire pɔ nson ne fa (1.75%) a onipa a ɔde sika remane no na ɔbɛtua, gye sɛ sikamaneɛ a ɛfiri amannɔne reba no na deɛ ne nsa bɛka sika no bɛtua saa ɛtoɔ yi.
english: The levy will cover mobile money payments, bank transfers, merchant payments, and inward remittances.

twi: Saa ɛtoɔ yi bɛhyɛ aseɛ wɔ Ɔgyefuo bosome da ɛdi kan wɔ afe 2022 mu.
english: The applicable rate levied on all these transactions is 1.75 percent, which will be borne by the sender, except for inward remittances where it will be borne by the recipient.

twi: Sikamaneɛ a ɛbɛkɔ so wɔ da koro mu a ɛduru sidi ɔha (GH¢100) anaa deɛ ɛnnuru saa no, ɛtoɔ yi nka no.
english: This will take effect 1st February, 2022. Transactions that add up to GH¢100 or less per day will be exempt from this levy.

twi: Nhyehyɛeɛ A Ɛfa Dwumadie Ho Sikasɛm Ho 15. Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛde sika bɛdi dwuma a ɛhia mapa na aboa ama yɛanya sikasɛm mu ahohyɛsoɔ enti, yɛbɛtu dwumadie ho sikasɛm nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ ho anammɔn wɔ afe 2022 ne mmerɛ kakra a ɛdi yɛn anim yi mu:
english: To contain expenditures and further enhance fiscal sustainability, a number of expenditure measures will be implemented in the 2022 fiscal year and the medium-term. a.

Afe 2022 mu ne mmerɛ kakra a ɛdi yɛn anim yi mu no, yɛbɛyɛ Aban adwumayɛfoɔ dwumadie nnyinasoɔ mu nhwehwɛmu nam so de ahunu adwumayɛfoɔ dodoɔ a wɔn ho bɛhia wɔ Aban nnwuma ahodoɔ mu sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a yɛbɛnya Aban adwumayɛfoɔ dodoɔ a ɛfata na wɔn dwumadie adi mu, c.
english: Government will continue to safeguard the integrity of the payroll system by ensuring that only public sector employees properly engaged through approved channels are placed on the payroll; b. a staff rationalisation exercise will be carried out in 2022 and the medium-term to instil efficiency in the allocation of staff to government institutions with the view to right-sizing the public sector workforce; c.

twi: Mpontunnwuma afoforɔ biara a yɛaka ho asɛm wɔ afe 2022 Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi mu sɛ yɛbɛyɛ, ne deɛ Aban Nnwuma (MDAs), Kuropɔn, Nkuro ne Mansini Mmarahyɛbadwa (MMDAs) ne Aban Nnwumakuo ahodoɔ (SOEs) no Animanim Mpontuo Nhyehyɛeɛ (Medium-Term Development Plans) mu no ho anammɔntuo nyinaa a ɛmfa ho ne baabi a dwumadie no ho sika firi no, yɛde bɛfa mmara (L.I. 2411) ɛkwan no so sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a yɛbɛyi sikasɛeɛ akwa na aboa ama ɔman mpontunneɛ ho dwumadie a Aban nnwuma di ma ɔmanfoɔ no adi mu ama mfasoɔ aba ho.
english: All new projects announced in the 2022 Budget and those included in the Medium-Term Development Plans of MDAs, MMDAs and SOEs shall, irrespective of their funding source, be subjected to the processes outlined in l.I. 2411 to ensure efficiency and effectiveness in the delivery of public infrastructure and provision of public goods and services.

twi: Yɛbɛdi sikasɛm ho anammɔntuo ahodoɔ a ɛdidi soɔ yi so sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a yɛremfom wɔ mmerɛ kakra a ɛdi yɛn anim yi mu wɔ sikasɛm ahohyɛsoɔ ɛkwan a yɛatwa ato hɔ no:
english: The following expenditure commitments control measures will also be enforced to avoid veering off the chartered medium-term fiscal consolidation path.

twi: Nneɛma a Aban Nnwuma agye atom wɔ wɔn Nneɛmatɔ Nhyehyɛeɛ (Procurement Plans) mu a apue edwa wɔ Aban Nneɛmatɔ Mpenesoɔ Adwumakuo (PPA) no abɛɛfo amaneɛbɔbea (website) no nko ara na yɛbɛdi ho dwuma de ama nneɛmatɔ ho kɔntraagye, Ɛsɛ sɛ Nneɛmatɔ ho abisadeɛ a Aban adwumakuo biara bɛyɛ wɔ afe biara mu no yɛ deɛ wɔatwa ɛho sika ato hɔ wɔ saa afe korɔ no mu Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ mu.
english: Only items specified in approved MDAs' Procurement Plans posted on the PPA website can be considered for procurement contracts; All procurement requests by procurement entities relating to a particular fiscal year must be backed by budgetary allocations approved for that year.

twi: Yei da nkyɛn a, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhunu baabi a saa nneɛmatɔ yi ho sika firi reba ɛnna sika dodoɔ a ɛwɔ hɔ ma saa nneɛmatɔ yi, Aban adwumam panin biara nni ho ɛkwan sɛ ɔde ne nsa hyɛ Nteaseɛ Apam (MoU) biara ase de kyekyere Ghana Aban wɔ sikasɛm mu wɔ ɛberɛ a ɔnnyee mpenesoɔ mfirii Ɔsoafoɔ a Ɔhwɛ Sikasɛm so no nkyɛn.
english: This notwithstanding, all such requests must also be based on actual confirmed sources and availability of funding; No public official must sign any MOU or agreement that commits the Government of Ghana financially without prior approval or clearance from the Minister for Finance.

twi: Ghana Covid-19 Asetɔre Ne Ankorankorɛ Nnwuma Mu Nkanyan Ho Mmoa (Ghanacares) “Obaatan Pa” Dwumadie No 17. Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛduru yɛn botaeɛ a yɛpɛ sɛ Ghana duru mpɛmpɛnsoɔ a yɛrenhia mmoa ho, na afei yɛasane agyina yɛn nan so wɔ COVID-19 Yadeɛ Kontonkurowi akyi enti, Ghana Aban hyɛɛ aseɛ tuu Ghana Covid-19 Asetɔre (GhanaCARES) "Obaatan Ne Ankorankorɛ Nnwuma Mu Nkanyan Ho Mmoa Pa- (GH¢100 Dwumadie a emu sikabotene yɛ sidi ɔpepepem ɔha baako billion) ho anammɔn.
english: To realise the vision of transforming Ghana Beyond Aid, and beyond COVID- 19 Pandemic, Government commenced the implementation of the GH¢100 billion Ghana COVID-19 Alleviation and Revitalisation of Enterprises Support programme, (the GhanaCARES “Obaatan pa” programme).

twi: Yei botaeɛ ne sɛ yɛnam ankorankorɛ nnwuma ho no nhyehyɛeɛ mu mpontuo ne mmoa a yɛde bɛma wɔn no so ama ɔman yi sikasɛm agyina yie, nkanyan aba mu na ɛnam so ama nsakraeɛ pa aba ɔmanfoɔ asetena mu.
english: This is to stabilise, revitalise and transform our nation, through the improvement of the business environment, and support the private sector.

twi: Deɛ ɛdidi soɔ yi ne dwumadie no mu nkonimdie ahodoɔ a epuee wɔ afe 2021 mu ɛnna afei anammɔn ahodoɔ a yɛasi gyinaeɛ sɛ yɛbɛtu wɔ afe 2022 mu.
english: The following are highlights of the key successes of the programme in 2021 and initiatives planned for 2022.

twi: Abɛɛfo Ɛkwan a Yɛfa so yɛ Kua ne Nnuanekra Nhyɛananmu 19. Ahineme bosome baa awieeɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu no, na yɛafa abɛɛfo ɛkwan so atwerɛ nnipa dodoɔ mpem ahanum aduɔson nkron, ahansia aduosia mmienu (579,662 individuals) edin a emu mpem ahanum aduanan nson, ɔha ne aduonu nsia yɛ akuafoɔ (547,126 farmers) ɛnna emu mpem aduasa mmienu, ahanum ne aduasa nsia yɛ nnipa a wɔdi dwuma ahodoɔ wɔ kua mu (32,536 value chain actors) na yei bɛboa ama yɛatumi de yɛn ani adi wɔn dwumadie akyi, ahunu obiara dwuma a ɔredi sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a, Aban mmoa a ɔde boa kuadwuma no bɛdi mu na emu ayɛ fann a obiara bɛhunu deɛ ɛrekɔ soɔ.
english: A total of 579,662 individuals, comprising 547,126 farmers and 32,536 value chain actors, have been registered in an electronic database of farmers as of October 2021, to improve tracking, targeting, efficiency and transparency in public support programmes within the agriculture sector.

twi: Aban ne nnipakuo ahodoɔ a wɔdi nkokɔyɛn, ɛmo, soya ne ntoosi ho dwuma no nyinaa hyiaeɛ, na ɛnam nhyiamu yi so maa Aban hunuu ɔhaw ahodoɔ a ɛwɔ wɔn dwumadie mu na yei maa Aban yɛɛ nhyehyɛeɛ a ɔnam so bɛma kuadwuma mu nnwumakuo ahodoɔ no bosea a ɛho nsiho wɔ fam sɛdeɛ wɔde bɛsɔ wɔn dwumadie mu ɔhaw ano.
english: Government engaged various actors in the poultry, rice, soya and tomato value-chain to understand the challenges of the sub-sector, which led to the development of a framework to provide Interest Rate Subsidy (IRS) to agribusinesses to address the financing constraints.

twi: Saa nhyehyɛeɛ yi mu no, wɔde bosea a wɔate ɛho nsiho no so ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduonum (50% subsidy on interest) bɛma kuadwuma mu nnwumakuo a wɔfata ama wɔde atotɔ dwumadie mu akadeɛ a wɔhia na wɔde atrɛ wɔn dwetire mu nso.
english: The IRS intervention will grant about 50 percent subsidy on interest charges for loans advanced to qualified agribusinesses to secure equipment and expand working capital.

english: To sustain the modernisation of agriculture, the following measures will be pursued in 2022. create a Ghana Agricultural land Information Bank (GhlIB) to improve access to land, especially for commercial farming; sensitise and engage the youth on the opportunities within the agricultural sector, including the use of social media; and map-out agribusiness start-up ecosystem and resources to take stock of the ecosystem resources and disseminate them to the youth

twi: Nsrahwɛ, Adwinnie Ne Amammerɛ Mpontuo 22. english: As part of promoting the Tourism, Art and Culture Sector of the economy under the CARES, Government completed the on boarding of 300 operators on the National Tourism Destination Single window platform to automate tourism operations and enhance service delivery and quality.

twi: Afe 2022 mu no, Aban bɛsisi mmeaeɛ bi te sɛ Adwinnie Mpontuo Beaeɛ, Anyinam mfidie, mfidie a asɛe akwaa beaeɛ, na wayiyi akwan a ɛkɔ nsrahwɛbea na afei ɔde mpontunneɛ bi te sɛ anyinam nkanea, nsuo ne nkratoɔ ne nkutahodie ho akadeɛ akɔ nsrahwɛbea ahodoɔ.
english: In 2022, Government will construct ancillary facilities such as a Pattern Development Shop, a Powerhouse, a Scrapyard, and road networks as well as provide other infrastructure such as power, water and telecommunication facilities at tourist sites.

twi: Adwadeɛyɔ ne Adwadeɛ a Yɛde bɛkɔ Amannɔne Mu Mpontuo 24. Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na dwuma a yɛbɛdi no ne Aban Mfidinnwuma ho Botaeɛ ahodoɔ Edu (Governmentqs 10-Point Industrialization Agenda) no bɛsiae soɔ enti, yɛasi gyinaeɛ sɛ yɛbɛma yɛn ani akɔ Ghana Mfidinnwuma Nketewa mu ntrɛmu so sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a, wɔbɛtumi ayɛ adwadeɛ a ɛbɛnya boɔ wɔ amannɔne edwa so, nnwuma a wɔdane mfudeɛ ani dwumadie bɛtu mpɔn, wɔayɛ adwadeɛ bebree a yɛde bɛkɔ amannɔne akɔtɔn na ɛnam so ama nnwuma abu so ma ɔmanfoɔ anya bi ayɛ.
english: In alignment with Government's 10-Point Industrialization Agenda, accelerated expansion of Ghana's light Manufacturing sector is prioritised to ensure rapid competitive import-substitution, expanded capacity for agroprocessing, increased exports and job creation.

twi: Afe 2021, Aban hyɛɛ aseɛ sii Aduyɛ Beaeɛ te sɛ deɛ ɛwɔ ewiase baabiara wɔ Noguchi sɛdeɛ ɛbɛboa ɔman yi mu nnuroyɛ nnwumakuo wɔ wɔn
english: In 2021, Government commenced works towards establishing the Bioequivalence Centre at Noguchi to support the local pharmaceutical manufacturing industry.

twi: Afe 2022 mu no, yɛbɛtu anammɔn a ɛdidi soɔ yi: Nnwumakuo ho nhyehyɛeɛ mu nsakraeɛ ahodoɔ no bɛyɛ ntɛmntɛm na abɛɛfo ɛkwan a wɔfa so di dwuma bɛdi akotene wɔ Nnwumakuo ho Nkrataayɛfoɔ Panin Adwumam (Registrar General Department), Aban bɛhyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ ase de asisi Mantam Mfidinnwuma Mmeaeɛ a wɔne Mfidinnwuma ho Nimdeɛ Asuapɔn ahodoɔ (Technical Universities) no bɛnya twaka, ɛnna afei Yɛbɛtrɛ nnuro a yɛtɔ firi ɔman yi mu nnuroyɛ nnwumakuo no hɔ mu na yɛne wɔn aka abom ayɛ adwuma ama wɔayɛ nnuro a ɛdi mu.
english: The following key initiatives will be implemented in 2022. Acceleration of Business Regulatory Reforms (including digitization of operations at the Registrar General Department; Commence a programme to build regional industrial parks linked to technical universities; and Expand domestic procurement of pharmaceuticals and work with industry to facilitate production of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API)

twi: Yɛreka ɛkwan a ɛda yɛne ewiase aman ntam wɔ abɛɛfo nimdeɛ mu no apua na yɛama abɛɛfo nkutahodie ho nhyehyɛeɛ ayɛ ntɛmntɛm 25. Aban gu so de nkɔsoɔ mapa reba yɛn abɛɛfo nkutahodie nhyehyɛeɛ ho anammɔntuo no mu.
english: Government is making significant progress towards our digitalisation drive.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na saa anammɔntuo yi bɛwie pɛyɛ enti, Aban ama Ghanafoɔ bɛboro ɔpepem dunum (over 15 million Ghanaians) anya wɔn ankasa ahyɛnsoɔ kaade na ɔde fidua ɔpepem nson ne mpem ahanum (7.5 million houses) nso ato ɔman abɛɛfo akyirikwan nhyehyɛeɛ no so a ɛboa ma yɛhunu beaeɛ a fidua ahodoɔ yi mu biara wɔ pɔtee. english: To this end, Government issued unique identification cards to over 15 million Ghanaians and placed 7.5 million houses on the national digital address system. 26. The drive to digitise the economy has received additional recognition from the adoption of the e-cedi currency by the Bank of Ghana. we have rolled out the oGhana.gov' platform as well as other initiatives to enhance and expand efficiency in service delivery. ”

english: Government has commenced concrete steps to establish the Ghana Vaccine Manufacturing Centre.

english: A draft National Vaccine Policy will be finalised and the establishment of a National Vaccine Institute to coordinate production of vaccines is underway.

twi: Aban nam ayaresabea ahodoɔ ɔha ne dubaako (Agenda 111 programme) a ɔrebɛsi wɔ mansini ahodoɔ mu no so ne Ɔman Apɔmuden Nsiakyibaa Nhyehyɛeɛ (National Health Insurance Scheme) bɛdi nsawɔsoɔ ama apɔmuden ho akadeɛ akɔ nkan na wama Apɔmuden mmeaeɛ no nsa aka sika a wɔhia de adi wɔn dwuma sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a apɔmuden a yɛrepɛ ama obiara wɔ afe 2030 mu no bɛba mu pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: In conjunction with the National Health Insurance Scheme, Government will under the Agenda 111 programme boost health care infrastructure and financial access to health care to achieve quality universal health coverage by the year 2030.

twi: Mmabunu adwumanya ne nsaanodwuma ho ɔhaw anosie 28. Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛtumi asi mmabunu adwumayɛ ne nsaanodwuma ho ɔhaw ano enti, Aban nam dwumadie ahodoɔ sɛ ebia NEIP, NABCO, Ɔman nnuadua dwumadie ne NBSSI (a seesei wɔfrɛ no GEA) no so abuebue nnwuma ho akwannya ato hɔ ama mmabunu ne nnwuma nketewa ne adantam (SMEs).
english: To help address the youth unemployment and skills challenge, Government through special programmes such as NEIP, NABCO, National Afforestation and NBSSI (now GEA), has created significant job opportunities for the youth and SMEs.

twi: Nkutahodie dodoɔ a akɔ so wɔ Aban ne akuhodoɔ a mmabunu ne nwomasua akuhodoɔ ka ho bie ntam enti no, afe 2022 yi mu no, Aban bɛgyina Ghana COVID-19 Asetɔre ne Ankorankorɛ Nnwuma mu Nkanyan ho mmoa (GhanaCARES) dwumadie no so afiri aseɛ atu nhyehyɛeɛ a ne edin de YouStart no ase, afa so de sikabotene a ano boɔ som ɔpepepem baako (Ghc 1.0 billion) nam so de abuebue nnwuma dodoɔ ɔpepem baako wɔ mfeɛ mmiɛnsa ntam.
english: Following extensive consultation with stakeholders, including youth associations and educational institutions, Government in 2022 will implement the YouStart Initiative as a vehicle to use GH¢1.0 billion to create 1 million jobs in 3 years under the GhanaCARES programme.

twi: YouStart dwumadie yi bɛboa wɔn a afei na wɔahyɛ wɔn ankasa nnwuma ase no ama wɔanya sika, anya mimdeɛ, anya nsaanodwuma ho nteteeɛ ne nkanyan de afiri wɔn ankasa nnwuma ase ama akɔ nkan.
english: The YouStart will support young entrepreneurs to gain access to capital, training, technical skills, and mentoring to enable them launch and operate their own businesses.

twi: Ewiem nsakraeɛ ho anammɔntuo ne ɛkwan pa a yɛrefa so abrɛ ewiem nneɛma bɔne ano ase. 30. COVID-19 akyiri sikasɛm nsiesie nhyehyɛeɛ no ama akwannya a yɛnam so bɛtumi afa ɛkwan pa ne nkoden so aduadua nnua nam so agyina yie bio.
english: The post COVID-19 economic recovery agenda provides an opportunity to build back better through innovation and more aggressive pursuit of green growth.

twi: Ne saa enti, Aban de ewiem nsakraeɛ ho nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ agu akwan mu a ɛbɛboa kankorɔ, sikasɛm mu mpontuo, adwumanya ne nnipa mu nyiyimu ano abrɛ ase.
english: In this regard, Government has put in place climate change interventions to leverage the drive towards a green transition in a manner that promotes sustainable growth, financial and fiscal stability, increased employment, and reduced inequality.

twi: Ghanaman reyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ nam so redi nnuadua ho dwuma a yɛnam so bɛhyɛ kwaeɛ a wɔatwa emu nnua nyinaa no anan mu.
english: Ghana is pursuing and implementing an aggressive afforestation programme and projects aimed at restoring lost forest cover.

twi: Yei enti, Aban retu anammɔn afa so asiesie nsase a asɛe no, ama yɛn kwaeɛ ne emu mmoadoma ho banbɔ, ntotoeɛ ne dwumadie ahodoɔ a ɛde mfasoɔ bɛba no adi mu.
english: In this regard, Government is embarking on programmes to reclaim our degraded lands to ensure the sustainable protection, management, production and development of forest and wildlife resources.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛdi nnuatwa ne kwaeɛsɛe ho ɔhaw so no enti, Ɔmanpanin dii ɔmanfoɔ anim ma yɛduaduaa nnua boro mpem nson wɔ Ayɛwohomumɔ wɔ afe 2021 mu. Yei boroo nnua mpem enum a na ɛsi ani so sɛ yɛbɛduadua wɔ nhyehyɛeɛ a wɔato edin Green Ghana no mu no so.
english: ” 32. To avert the challenge of deforestation and forest degradation, H.E the President led the country to plant over seven million trees in June 2021. This was far above the five million targeted under the Green Ghana Project.

english: Following the expiration of Ghana's Medium-Term National Development Policy Framework (2018-2021), 2022 marks the country's transition into the Medium-Term National Development Policy Framework (MTNDPF) (2022-

english: The new Framework is anchored on the long-Term National Development Framework (Ghana@100), Coordinated Programme of Economic and Social Development Policies (2017-2024), Ghana Beyond Aid Agenda and Strategy, and Ghana COVID-19 Alleviation and Revitalisation of Enterprises Support Programme (GhanaCARES).

twi: Saa nhyehyɛeɛ yi botaeɛ foforɔ ne sɛ ɛbɛma yɛatumi aduru Amanaman Nkabom Ekuo nhyehyɛeɛ a wɔato edin "Agenda 2030- (SDGs) ne Abibirem Nkabom Botaeɛ a wɔato edin "Africa Union Agenda 2063- no ho.
english: This Framework also seeks to achieve the objectives of the UN Agenda 2030 (SDGs) and Africa Union Agenda 2063.

english: This section highlights the performance of Government in key areas and sectors of the economy in 2021, as well as programmes and activities for implementation in 2022.

english: Government, in its efforts to reduce unemployment levels, continues to implement policies and programmes such as the Ghana Productive Safety Net Project (GPSNP).

Kyekyɛɛ sika dodoɔ ɔpepem enum ne mpem aduɔwɔtwe mmienu GH¢5.82) maa fidua ahodoɔ ɔpepem nkron ahanu ne adunan ɛnan (9,244) a wɔwɔ mpɔtam ahodoɔ ɔha ne aduonu nwɔtwe mu (128 communities) wɔ Nkuropɔn, Nkuro ne Mansini aduanan baako (41 MMDAs) a ɛwɔ Atifi Amantam enum mu sɛ wɔmfa nhyɛ nnwuma ase anaa wɔmfa ntrɛ wɔn nnwuma no mu.
english: Under this project, Government. provided jobs for 33,952 extreme poor persons in 80 MMDAs with a total wage payout of GH¢53.43 million; and disbursed a total of GH¢5.82 million to 9,244 beneficiary households from 128 communities in 41 MMDAs in the five northern regions to commence businesses or expand their trade.

english: In line with Government's objective to direct young men and women into productive ventures, reduce the rate of rural-urban migration and improve livelihoods of the youth, 130,000 jobs were created through the rehabilitation and replanting, mass spraying, fertiliser application, hand pollination, mass pruning and cocoa farm irrigation in the cocoa sector. english: The National Afforestation Programme (NAP) provided an opportunity to engage a total of 72,000 persons exceeding the target of 60,000 to assist in various areas of planting activities.

english: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) engaged 82,869 beneficiaries under the various YEA modules.

english: “The Job Centre”, which links job seekers to potential employers, enabled 1,185 persons to gain employment.

english: From 2017 to date, a total of 278 1D1F projects are at various stages of implementation, out of which 106 companies are currently in operation, 148 are under construction while 24 constitute pipeline projects.

english: To date, the companies in operation have created 156,782 direct and indirect jobs, 17,451 of which were created in 2021.

english: In addition, 3.7 million seedlings, including ” Ofram, Emire, wawa, kokrodua, Teak, Cedrela, Gmelina, Cassia, Eucalyptus and Mahogany species were planted.

twi: Ɛnam dwumadie a wɔato edin sɛ "Galamstop- no so ama asutene akɛseɛ bi te sɛ, Asuo Pra a ɛwɔ Twifo Praso, Asuo Pra a ɛwɔ Daboase, Asuo Ankobra a ɛwɔ Bonsaso, Asuo Tano a ɛwɔ Elubo, Asuo Birim a ɛwɔ Osino ne Asuo Birim a ɛwɔ Bunso nyinaa ani ate nwann.

twi: Yɛhyɛɛ beaeɛ a wɔgya to hɔ de bɔ atenaeɛ ho ban ase wɔ mpɔtam ahodoɔ bi mu wɔ Firaw tadeɛ (Black and White Volta), Tano, Offin ne Densu, dii dwuma ahodoɔ pii a wɔnam so tetee ntutim ho nnipa dodoɔ ahanu aduonum mmienua (252 nursery attendants) wɔ mpɔtam nson mu, na afei yɛduaduaa nnua nketewa mpem dunsia, ahankron ne aduasa nson (16,937 seedlings).
english: Buffer zone restoration schemes were initiated in selected communities within the Black and white Volta, Tano, Offin and Densu basins with a variety of activities, including training of 252 nursery attendants in 7 communities, and planting of 16,937 tree seedlings.

twi: Yei nyinaa botaeɛ ne sɛ ɛbɛboa ahyɛ atenaeɛ a agyigya wɔ asuo ho no na ate ɔhaw a nnipa dwumadie de aba asuo ahodoɔ no ho no so.

twi: Yeinom na ɛdidi soɔ yi: Atifi Apueeɛ Mantam nsuo ho dwumadie ɔfa a ɛdi kan (a nnipa a wɔwɔ Navrongo, Bolgatanga, Paga, Bongo ne ne mpɔtam bɛnya ho mfasoɔ) – wɔadi ɛho dwuma akɔduru ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduɔkron nwɔtwe (98 % completed) na wɔbɛpa ɛho ntoma wɔ Ɔpɛnimma bosome mu wɔ afe 2021 mu, Tamale Nsuo Dwumadie – yɛawie ɛho ntotoeɛ a ɛho dwumadie rebɛfiri aseɛ, Damango Nsuo Dwumadie – ɛho adrɔɔdrɔɔ ne nhyehyɛeɛ nyinaa adi mu a ɛrebɛfiri aseɛ, Wenchi Nsuo Dwumadie – yɛawie ɛho nhyehyɛeɛ nyinaa ama dwumadie no afiri aseɛ, Keta Nsuo Dwumadie – yɛawie ɛho nhyehyɛeɛ nyinaa ama dwumadie no gu so., ɛnna Sekondi-Takoradi Nsuo Dwumadie – yɛawie ɛho dwumadie nyinaa de nsa ahyehyɛ ɛho kɔntraagye ase.
english: They include the following. Upper East Region water Supply Project Phase I (covering Navrongo, Bolgatanga, Paga, Bongo and its environs) a 98 percent completed and scheduled for commissioning in December 2021; Tamale water Supply Project a VFM completed to pave way for commencement of the Project; Damango water Supply Project a Initial designs and VFM completed; wenchi water Supply Project a VFM completed and project commenced; keta water Supply Project a VFM completed and works ongoing; and Sekondi-Takoradi water Supply Project a VFM completed and contract signed.

twi: Ɛduruu Ɛbɔ bosome da a ɛtɔ so aduasa wɔ afe 2021 mu no, na wɔatwerɛ Ghanafoɔ dodoɔ ɔpepem dunum, mpem ahansia aduonum nsia, ɔha ne aduosia (15,656,160 Ghanaians) edin wɔ Ɔmanbayɛ ho Adansedie Nwoma (National Identity Register (NIR) no mu, na wɔmaa saa nnipa yi mu dodoɔ ɔpepem dubaako, mpem ahansia aduanan nwɔtwe ne ahasa aduɔkron baako (11,648,391 Ghanaians) a na wɔadi boro mfeɛ dunum nyinaa Ɔman Kaade no bi (Ghana Cards).
english: Water Reservoir in Novrongo Th 54. As at 30 September, 2021, 15,656,160 Ghanaians were enrolled on the National Identity Register (NIR), out of which 11,648,391 Ghanaians aged 15 years and above were issued with Ghana Cards.

english: A total of 163,695 foreigners were also enrolled and issued with Non-Citizen Identity Cards.

twi: Wɔfirii Ɔman SIM kaade ho edintwerɛ nhyehyɛeɛ no ase wɔ Ahinime bosome ɛda a ɛdi kan wɔ 2021 mu wɔ nɛtwork ahodoɔ no nyinaa so, na ɛbɛboa asi SIM kaade ho korɔnobɔ ne "mobael- fon a wɔde di dwuma a ɛmfa mmarakwan so no ano, na saa dwumadie yi bɛba awieeɛ wɔ Ɔbɛnem bosome awieeɛ wɔ 2022 mu.
english: The National SIM Card Registration programme, which is expected to reduce st SIM fraud and use of mobile phones for illegal activities, commenced on 1 st October, 2021 on all networks and is expected to end on 31 March, 2022.

twi: Ɛduruu Ɛbɔ bosome awieeɛ wɔ afe 2021 mu no, na yɛayɛ ɛberɛ ano ɛberɛ ano nsiesie wɔ lɔre akwan a ɛka nkuro akɛseɛ bom kwansini mpem aduonu baako, ahansia ne enum (21,165 km), deɛ ɛkɔ beaeɛ a mfudeɛ firi ba kwansini mpem nsia, ahanu aduosia enum (6,265 km) ne kurom akwan kwansini mpem mmienu, ahankron ne aduasa nson (2,937 km).
english: As at the end of September 2021, routine maintenance was carried out on 21,165km of the trunk road network, 6,265km of the feeder road network, and 2,937km of the urban road network.

twi: Kutawonsa da a ɛtɔ so Nkron wɔ afe 2021 mu no, yɛpaa Pokuase lɔre ɛkwan abɔnta nsamsoɔ ho dwumadie a abɔntanan nsamsoɔ, lɔre akwan bi a wɔahyɛda ayiyi ato hɔ kwansini dummienu, beaeɛ a ɔmanfoɔ fa so wɔ lɔrekwan ho, ɛtwene a nnipa fa so, ɛtwene a nnipa fa aseɛ ne suka ahodoɔ ka ho no ho ntoma.

twi: Afei yɛbɛwie akwan a ɛka nkuro akɛseɛ bɔ mu kwansini aduɔson enum (75km), deɛ ɛkɔ baabi a mfudeɛ firi ba kwansini ɔha aduonum (150 km) ne kurom akwan kwansini aduasa (30 km) ho dwumadie.
english: Rehabilitation works on 75km of trunk roads, 150km of feeder roads and 30km of urban roads will also be undertaken.

Phase 2 of the Obetsebi lamptey Circle Interchange; rd Phase 2 of the 3 Tier of the Tema Motorway Roundabout interchange; The la Beach Road Project (lots 102) on the Accra-Tema Beach Road; and Development works on the kumasi lake Roads and Drainage Extension Project.

english: Under the Ghana Productive Safety Net Project (GPSNP), Government distributed a total of 7.9 million cash crop seedlings to farmers under the “Planting for Export and Rural Development” (PERD) Programme.

english: PERD Seedlings for Farmers at kintampo in Bono East Region ” 64. Government under the “Planting for Export and Rural Development” initiative, distributed 1,360,589 cashew, coffee, coconut, oil palm, mango and rubber seedlings to 7,543 farmers in Ahafo, Ashanti, Bono, Central, Eastern, Greater Accra, Oti, western, western North and Volta Regions.

english: Additionally, Government distributed 7,700,500 vaccines for the control of poultry and livestock diseases.

english: Government continued rehabilitation and modernisation of the following irrigation projects, which when completed will make available a total irrigation area of 6,766ha and ensure all-year-round crop production. kpong Irrigation Scheme (2,176ha); Tono Irrigation Scheme (2,490ha); and kpong left Bank Irrigation Project (2,100ha).
